title: MZ Event cut off in Game

posts.author: AltoRosei
posts.body:
Hello, I have been using RPG Maker for a while now. Up to this point, I never had an issue like this. Normally, event cutoffs are an easy fix with Photoshop or any other photo editor program. However, this is the first time, no matter how many times I try to edit the image and attempt different 48x48 pixels. Always with the event tab, it shows the flowers fitting fine and not cut off; however, when I play my game, for some reason the flowers are so badly cut off. I tried multiple different edits to get around it, thinking it just might be the game running the file wrong or maybe the file grid was off, but I am not sure. I'm so confused about how to fix this. Any help would be great or anyone able to fix it would be very appreciated. I'll also attach my flowers down below, as the goal was to make a small animation with them.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body: Events don't have shadows by default. Are you using any plugins? If so, maybe one of them adds "sinking" or "submerged" effects to characters on certain tiles and/or regions. I suggest sharing screenshot(s) of your Plugin Manager, showing all plugins you're using and their load order.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
All good, there's no rush~
To confirm whether it's a plugin responsible, you could try turning them all off in the Plugin Manager (uncheck all the boxes), save your project to apply plugin changes, then test. (Choose New Game, or skip the title screen; don't continue from a previous save.) If your flowers display normally with plugins off, then you can try turning some plugins back on, save, test, and repeat until you've narrowed it down.
Personally I'm not very familiar with VisuStella's plugins, so I'm not sure if they have something like that...maybe someone else will know more.

posts.author: fizzly
posts.body:
Are you sure the name of the file is correct? Did you put "$" as a prefix for that file?
If yes, then it must be some plugins fault for 90%. Try to disable one by one and check.
